# task-c9599e63: noisy rectangular patches

## Validated rule

The grid has a background color and multiple rectangular patches, which may use different colors. Each patch is intended to be uniform. Some cells inside a patch may be overwritten by unrelated colors; restore them to the patch's color. Scattered non-background pixels outside the intended rectangles are distractors/noise and should be reset to the background. Preserve dimensions and valid patch cells.

Infer each rectangle from the visible consistent-color regions and its rectangular bounds. Use all patch colors, not just the largest or most frequent one. Noise inside a rectangle is corrected to the rectangle color; noise outside rectangles is cleared to background. Do not indiscriminately erase small patches or original colors that make valid rectangles.

## Evidence from three demos

- Demo 1 (27x10): background 1, color-6 rectangles at rows 2–5/cols 3–7, rows 7–13/cols 1–6, rows 17–21/cols 2–5, and rows 24–26/cols 6–8 (zero-indexed). - Demo 2 (13x28): background 5; color-4 rectangles included rows 2–3/cols 4–5 and rows 3–8/cols 11–14; a color-2 rectangle occupied rows 3–9/cols 25–27. Embedded 1/9 anomalies in these rectangles were restored to patch color. Isolated noise outside patches was reset to 5.

Other isolated non-background noise was reset to 5.

These demos establish multiple patch colors and sizes, with both interior corruption and external distractors. Do not assume every isolated non-background pixel is a patch seed.
